---
title: "Simulation Conventions"
description: "Read SCNSim complex responses with explicit phasors, current directions, wave references, loads, selected Views, and frequency units."
---

Before reading a phase, pole, or matrix entry, identify the Plan, selected View,
ordered axes, and frequency convention. This page connects the physical
conventions to SCNSim's version-bound Results. It does not change a circuit,
select a View automatically, or establish numerical accuracy from a plot.

## Quick reference

| Readout | Convention or boundary |
|---|---|
| Phasor / derivative | $e^{-i\omega t}$; $d/dt\mapsto-i\omega$; $\omega=2\pi f$ |
| Voltage / current | Voltage relative to Plan ground; terminal current into the DUT |
| S/Y/Z axes | Output row, input column; $I=YV$, $V=ZI$, $b=Sa$ |
| Wave reference | Real-positive or real-SPD reference; principal matrix square root |
| Loads and PTC | Source de-embedding, omitted unPTC matched loads, and explicit physical resistors are distinct; only named nonloading probes receive PTC |
| Public network / roots | S/Y/Z share one explicit View; loaded operator/root boundaries are distinct |
| Pole linewidth | Passive $\operatorname{Im}\Omega<0$; $\kappa=-2\operatorname{Im}\Omega$; a transfer zero is not a linewidth |
| Phase / dB | Wrapped argument; $20\log_{10}|S|$; positive delay has positive propagation phase |
| HB boundary | One conjugation, same signed-mode permutation, $\sqrt{|\omega|}$ normalization |

## Phasors, Fourier transforms, and units {#phasors-and-units}

SCNSim uses the real signal represented by

$$
x(t)=\operatorname{Re}\{X(\omega)e^{-i\omega t}\},\qquad
\frac{d}{dt}\longmapsto-i\omega.
$$

The matching Fourier pair is

$$
X(\omega)=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}x(t)e^{+i\omega t}\,dt,\qquad
x(t)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}X(\omega)e^{-i\omega t}\,d\omega.
$$

Ordinary frequency $f$ is in Hz and angular frequency $\omega=2\pi f$ is in
rad/s. A numerical value in GHz is not an angular frequency in rad/s. Public
quantities carry units; use the Result's frequency unit instead of inferring it
from a variable name.

Voltage is relative to the Plan's canonical reference ground. Terminal current
is positive **into the DUT**. With these choices, the elementary impedances and
admittances are

| Element | Impedance $Z$ | Admittance $Y$ |
|---|---|---|
| Resistor $R$ | $R$ | $1/R$ |
| Capacitor $C$ | $1/(-i\omega C)$ | $-i\omega C$ |
| Inductor $L$ | $-i\omega L$ | $1/(-i\omega L)=i/(\omega L)$ |

The signs follow from the phasor, not from which way a symbol faces in a
schematic. A delayed signal has $X_{\rm out}=e^{+i\omega\tau}X_{\rm in}$ for
positive delay $\tau$ under this convention.

## Matrix axes and power waves {#matrix-axes-and-power-waves}

For ordered terminal voltage and current vectors,

$$
I=YV,\qquad V=ZI,\qquad b=Sa.
$$

Every matrix uses **output row, input column**. Thus $S_{21}$ is outgoing wave
at terminal 2 due to incident wave at terminal 1, with other incident waves
zero. A named `SParameterTrace(input_port=..., output_port=...)` binds those
roles; it does not change the matrix order. Read `.s.view` and the Result's
Port/channel metadata before interpreting a numeric index. For a four-Port
matrix, a named left-to-right channel need not occupy row 2, column 1.

For real positive scalar references, let
$R_0=\operatorname{diag}(Z_{01},\ldots,Z_{0N})$ and $D=R_0^{1/2}$. More
generally, the supported matrix reference is real symmetric positive definite
(SPD), with its unique real-SPD **principal matrix square root** $D$:

$$
a=\tfrac12(D^{-1}V+DI),\qquad
b=\tfrac12(D^{-1}V-DI).
$$

This is not an elementwise square root or an arbitrary Cholesky factor. With
$\widetilde Y=DYD$ and $\widetilde Z=D^{-1}ZD^{-1}$, where the required solves
exist,

$$
S=(I+\widetilde Y)^{-1}(I-\widetilde Y)
 =(\widetilde Z+I)^{-1}(\widetilde Z-I).
$$

Conversely,

$$
Y=D^{-1}(I+S)^{-1}(I-S)D^{-1},\qquad
Z=D(I-S)^{-1}(I+S)D.
$$

These formulas name linear solves, not a requirement to allocate a full inverse
in the implementation. Renormalizing the wave reference changes $S$ while
leaving terminal $Y,Z$ unchanged **when the physical network and boundary stay
fixed**. A changed omitted matched termination can change the effective retained
network and its Y/Z. Adding or removing a resistor changes the network instead.

A real invertible voltage-coordinate change $V_m=AV$ has dual current
$I_m=A^{-T}I$, so

$$
Y_m=A^{-T}YA^{-1},\qquad Z_m=AZA^T,\qquad R_{0m}=AR_0A^T.
$$

The transpose is the **ordinary transpose**, not the complex-conjugate
transpose. The transformed wave coordinates use $D_m=R_{0m}^{1/2}$ and
$Q=D_m^{-1}AD$, giving $S_m=QSQ^T$. A transformed reference can have
non-diagonal entries even when the original references were diagonal. This
mathematical relation does not expand the public `transform_pair()` API to
arbitrary user matrices.

### Formula-only example: 100 ohm DUT, 50 ohm reference

For one resistor DUT $Z_{\rm DUT}=100\,\Omega$ and wave reference
$Z_0=50\,\Omega$,

$$
Y_{\rm DUT}=0.01\,\mathrm S,\qquad
S_{11}=\frac{100-50}{100+50}=\frac13.
$$

If a separate $50\,\Omega$ shunt is actually included in a returned **loaded**
terminal operator, its admittance is instead
$Y_{\rm loaded}=0.01+0.02=0.03\,\mathrm S$ and its impedance is
$100/3\,\Omega$. The wave reference alone does not create that shunt. Removing
it requires its actual stamp and removal authority; subtracting $1/Z_0$ from
an already de-embedded DUT admittance would be wrong. This is an algebraic
example, not a simulated fixture or accuracy claim.

## Loads, de-embedding, PTC, and retention {#loads-and-selected-views}

Three operations must remain distinct:

| Boundary | Meaning in SCNSim |
|---|---|
| Backend source resistor | A solver boundary stamp. SCNSim de-embeds it when forming the selected public network; it is not a second physical DUT resistor. |
| Omitted matched Port | A declared, uncompensated Port omitted from the selected scattering boundary retains its matched termination. An explicitly PTC-compensated omitted probe does not retain that removed load. |
| Explicit physical resistor | Part of the authored physical circuit; it remains. PTC does not remove an explicit physical resistor. |

Selective Port-Termination Compensation (PTC) removes only the proven load
stamp of each explicitly supplied `PortRef` with role `nonloading_probe`.
A name such as “probe” does not authorize subtraction. The selected
`ReductionPipeline().ptc(...)` is the authority; SCNSim does not infer PTC from
a plot, coordinate name, or the choice of Y rather than S.

`retain()` selects and orders a boundary. It does **not** unload omitted
measurement Ports, compensate probes, or remove physical resistors. PTC and
retention therefore answer different questions and their order remains in the
View lineage.

### Two measurement Ports and two probes

Consider a Plan with measurement Ports `feedline_in`, `feedline_out` and two
actual `nonloading_probe` PortRefs `probe_plus`, `probe_minus`:

```python
raw_view = run.original
selected_view = raw_view.reduce(
    ReductionPipeline()
    .ptc(probe_plus, probe_minus)
    .retain("feedline_in", "feedline_out")
)
```

This declaration removes exactly the two probe load stamps and keeps the
feedline pair as the scattering boundary. Measurement termination effects and
any explicit physical resistors still follow their declared roles. A pipeline
with only `retain()` is a different network question. The illustration declares
no component values, sample grid, or numerical Result.

## Public S/Y/Z versus loaded operators {#network-versus-loaded-operator}

For a Port-realizable View, the public `.s`, `.y`, and `.z` surfaces describe
**one selected network**, with the same explicit View and ordered boundary.
Backend source admittances are de-embedded from that public network; omitted
matched terminations remain where required. PTC, if requested, applies to all
three surfaces consistently.

Root, pole, coupling, and operator requests ask about their declared selected
**loaded operator**, not automatically the same source-de-embedded scattering
network. Non-Port coordinate Y/Z quantities also belong to their declared
coordinate/operator boundary. Retaining one coordinate can leave external
loads active. Read the Spec, View lineage, quantity family, and axis bindings
before comparing it to a Port-network Y/Z entry.

::: {.callout-important title="No automatic reporting-policy PTC"}
The upstream SCQ Design network-trace procedure uses raw S and
evidence-authorized PTC Y/Z as its project reporting defaults. Those defaults
are not an automatic SCNSim View operation. In SCNSim the supplied View governs
S, Y, and Z together; `run.original` does not silently compensate Y/Z while
leaving S raw. Label both the selected View and any upstream post-processing.
:::

See [coordinates and Views](compilation-coordinates-and-network-views.qmd),
[the selected-network implementation](../implementation/view-lineage-and-selected-networks.qmd),
and [the Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd#common-matrix-surface)
for the version-bound API and failure rules.

## Complex roots, linewidth, and plots {#roots-linewidth-and-plots}

A freely decaying passive mode has

$$
\Omega=\omega_r-i\kappa/2,\qquad
 e^{-i\Omega t}=e^{-i\omega_rt}e^{-\kappa t/2}.
$$

Thus $\operatorname{Im}\Omega<0$ for positive decay,
$\kappa=-2\operatorname{Im}\Omega$, and the corresponding linewidth in Hz is
$\kappa/(2\pi)=-2\operatorname{Im}[\Omega/(2\pi)]$. A loaded root's linewidth
is not automatically intrinsic loss or a specific external-channel linewidth.
An ideal undamped root may have zero imaginary part. The imaginary part of a
**transfer zero** does not define a mode linewidth, even when it is zero or
very small; a zero and a pole solve different equations.

A magnitude plot in dB uses $20\log_{10}|S_{ij}|$ for the dimensionless wave
amplitude. Wrapped phase is the argument of the complex response, shown modulo
one turn (usually in degrees). Its branch-cut jump is not a discontinuity of
the circuit. Neither an S-magnitude dip nor a phase jump alone defines a
certified complex root, pole, or transfer zero.

## HB adapter boundary {#hb-adapter-boundary}

JosephsonCircuits' HB boundary uses the conjugate phasor convention. SCNSim
translates complete native S and return-Z once, using the **same signed
physical-frequency mode permutation** on both. With source convention $+$ and
SCNSim convention $-$, the normalization is

$$
M^-_{\rm native,phys}
 =W_{\rm out}\left[\Pi_{\rm out}M^+_{\rm JC}\Pi_{\rm in}^{T}\right]^*
 W_{\rm in}^{-1},\qquad
 W=\operatorname{diag}\sqrt{|\omega|},
$$

for either native matrix $M$. Conjugation does not transpose Port indices, and
signed tuples are not reversed a second time. The $\sqrt{|\omega|}$ factors
translate the backend normalization; they do not imply gain or loss. The
adapter then performs its declared source de-embedding and selected View
operations before forming public S/Y/Z. Consumers must not conjugate again.
Direct and HB grids remain independent; equal-looking curves do not establish
complex agreement at undeclared or mismatched frequencies. See
[Direct and HB](direct-and-hb-realizations.qmd) and
[HB realization](../implementation/hb-realization-and-outcomes.qmd#derive-one-selected-network-per-case).
